newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-MCGRATH ADDS TO LARA'S TEST WOES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-MCGRATH ADDS TO LARA'S TEST WOES.

text.p: Fast bowler Glenn McGrath hauled Australia out of trouble against West Indies in the third test on Friday as Brian Lara added to a wretched run of low scores.
McGrath claimed three wickets, including Lara's prized scalp, during 21 overs of sustained hostility at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.
At tea on the second day, West Indies were 154 for five in 74 overs in reply to Australia's first innings 219.
After watching the top order batsmen attempt to grind out their runs, wicketkeeper Junior Murray opted instead for aggression to remain 29 not out.
Jimmy Adams was the other not-out batsman on 23 after the pair added 47 runs in an unbroken sixth-wicket partnership.

Lara, who has yet to score a century on tour, played a rash cut shot to be dismissed for two before lunch, taking his tally of runs to a meagre 75 in five test innings. Lara holds the world records for highest test and first-class batting scores.

McGrath, who has removed Lara four times in the series to date, struck with his fourth ball to the left-hander when he lured him to slice a catch to Shane Warne in the gully. McGrath finished the session with figures of three for 32 in 21 overs.
West Indies, who trail 2-0 in the five-test series, resumed on 29 for one. Number three Shivnarine Chanderpaul scored 58 in a resilient innings before scooping a return catch to McGrath.
